requirements.requirement: Restore node1 through node4 to a valid common rsyslog package, configuration, and service state listening for TCP syslog on port 5514.
requirements.summary: All four final audits show required packages installed, identical validated rsyslog configuration, rsyslog enabled and active, and rsyslogd listening on TCP/5514 over IPv4 and IPv6. Independent lifecycle snapshots confirm the final listeners.

requirements.requirement: Correct security drift so the required TCP/5514 service and application log operate under the systems' security controls.
requirements.summary: Every node remains SELinux Enforcing, maps TCP/5514 to syslogd_port_t, permits 5514/tcp in runtime and permanent firewalld policy, and verifies the configuration and log-file contexts. Node1's pre-existing tmp_t log label was corrected and successfully retested.

requirements.requirement: On every node, accept a peer-originated TCP local0 message on port 5514 and write it to /var/log/infraset-app.log.
requirements.summary: Peer sends completed for all four targets, and each target's final audit directly found its unique local0 token in the application log. The audits also found no copy in /var/log/messages. Node1's initial label-related failure was repaired before a successful retry and final audit.

requirements.requirement: Preserve /var/lib/infraset-app/data/records.db on node1 through node4 while remediating drift.
requirements.summary: Each node's final SHA-256 hash and root:root 0640 metadata match its prepared baseline; the more detailed executor comparisons also retain size, inode, and modification time.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied on node1 through node4: rsyslog is valid and active on TCP/5514, security policy permits it while SELinux remains enforcing, peer local0 delivery reaches the requested log, and every records.db is preserved.
limitations: No reboot was performed; post-reboot persistence is supported by enabled services and permanent configuration but was not behaviorally exercised.
Functional routing was tested with one peer-generated local0.info token per node rather than an exhaustive severity or load test.
Lifecycle hygiene snapshots use bounded inventories and cannot exclude artifacts outside their observation scope.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-selinux-state
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-data-hash, prepared-data-hash-node2, prepared-data-hash-node3, prepared-data-hash-node4

operational_hygiene.summary: No executor-caused failed services, package inconsistency, or abandoned temporary artifacts are evident. The newly exposed TCP/5514 listeners are required by the task; the temporary-directory differences are transient systemd-private hostnamed directories.
